sources.entry: JankyBorders - A lightweight window border system for macOS. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/FelixKratz/JankyBorders) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: JankyBorders is a lightweight macOS tool that draws colored borders around windows to highlight the focused one, without using the accessibility API.
summary.what_it_does: Adds colored borders to user windows on macOS 14.0 and later. It highlights the currently focused window and says it does this without relying on the accessibility API, which it claims makes it faster than comparable tools. Border appearance is set through command-line options such as active_color, inactive_color, width, style, and hidpi. The options can be changed while a running instance is active by launching a new borders command with the new values. Settings can also be placed in a config file at ~/.config/borders/bordersrc, which runs automatically when borders starts with no arguments. The README points to a man page (man borders) and a Wiki for full option documentation.
use_cases: highlight the focused window on macOS
add colored window borders on a Mac
show which window has focus in a tiling setup
run window borders as a background service via brew
notable: Draws borders without the accessibility API, which the README says makes it faster than comparable tools
Options can be changed on a running instance by launching borders again with new values
Documented bootstrap examples for yabai and AeroSpace
caveats: Installation is shown only through Homebrew in the README
Full option list is in the man page and Wiki, not the README itself
